body.statement: Equip \(\Theta_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{leg}}\) with the Euclidean topology relative to \(t_2=t_1+x-y\) and its strict bridge-rank, moment, selector-variance, and ATT-variance inequalities. For any fixed \(\kappa<2\), \(\nu<13/40\), and \(C_{\mathrm{mom}}\) exceeding the \(8+\delta_0\) Gaussian moments at the displayed points, the symmetric point \(\theta=(1,1,1,1,1,1,r,1,1)\), for any fixed \(r>0\), is legal and has \(\rho_1=-\rho_2\), a nonzero selected limiting mean, and exact symmetric coverage for every local gap. At the asymmetric legal point \(\theta=(1,1,1/10,1/5,9/5,1/10,1/10,9/5,1/5)\), the primitive formulas give \(B=2\), \(R=4\), \(\eta=K=1/2\), \(\sigma_D^2=161/100\), \(c_{D1}=-19/100\), \(c_{D2}=91/100\), \(V_1=13/40\), and \(V_2=249/200\), so \(\rho_1=-0.262663049718703\) and \(\rho_2=0.6427525060282437\). With \(d/\sigma_D=-1\), equivalently \(k=1\), and \(z=\Phi^{-1}(0.95)\), substitution in \(C_z(k)\) gives \(C_z(1)=0.8858209104904335\) to the displayed numerical precision. The local scale \(t_{2,n}=t_2-(R^2/B^2)d/\sqrt n=1/5-4d/\sqrt n\) realizes that drift while preserving both bridge equalities and every strict legality margin eventually. Continuity of \(\Gamma(\theta,d)=(k,\rho_1,\rho_2,V_1,V_2)\), positivity at that asymmetric point, and the strict inequality \(\rho_1^2<\rho_2^2\) yield a relatively open neighborhood of legal local arrays with strict undercoverage; exchanging the role labels yields the opposite strict squared-correlation ordering, while reversing the drift sign yields strict overcoverage.
body.justification: Primitive realization prevents the Gaussian frontier from being an unattainable covariance thought experiment.
body.gap: Generic post-selection examples do not verify simultaneous proximal bridge validity, ridge-loss calibration, and positive ATT and selector variances inside a panel law.
body.consumer: The asymmetric family provides a calibrated stress test for a two-role proximal synthetic-control implementation.
body.proof_tex:
We first derive, rather than assume, the properties of the construction in \(\texttt{def:primitive-gaussian-family}\).  Give role one donor \(W_{1t}=c_1(F_t+e_{1t})\) and proxy \(W_{2t}=c_{2,n}(F_t+e_{2t})\), and exchange these assignments for role two.  At the tied limit, write \(c_j=t_j^{-1/2}\).  Independence and \(B=\mathbb E_nF_t^2=\mu^2+f\) give, for both roles,
\[
 M_s=c_1c_2B,
 \qquad
 \alpha_1=\frac{c_2B}{c_1c_2B}=\frac1{c_1},
 \qquad
 \alpha_2=\frac{c_1B}{c_1c_2B}=\frac1{c_2}.
\]
Therefore
\[
 Y_t(0)-W_{1t}\alpha_1=e_{0t}-e_{1t},
 \qquad
 Y_t(0)-W_{2t}\alpha_2=e_{0t}-e_{2t},
\]
and both residuals have mean zero.  This proves both bridge equations and \(\texttt{ass:bridge-centering}\).  Moreover, \(\Delta_t=\tau+\xi_t\) implies \(\mathbb E_n\Delta_t=\tau\), so for either role
\[
 \mathbb E_n\{Y_t(0)+\Delta_t-W_{jt}\alpha_j\}=\tau.
\]
Thus the observed residual mean identifies the causal target in this family; the equality is a consequence of the bridge calculation, not a definition of \(\tau\).  Since the bridge matrix is scalar, its singular value is
\[
 |M_s|=c_1c_2B=\frac{B}{\sqrt{t_1t_2}},
\]
which is strictly larger than \(\kappa\) on \(\Theta_{\mathcal G}^{\mathrm{leg}}\).

For a donor \(W_j=c_j(F+e_j)\), its population ridge coefficient satisfies
\[
 a_j=\frac{c_jB}{1+c_j^2(B+\operatorname{Var}(e_j))},
 \qquad
 W_j a_j
 =\frac{B}{t_j+B+\operatorname{Var}(e_j)}(F+e_j).
\]
The equality \(t_2=t_1+x-y\) makes both denominators equal to
\(R=t_1+B+x=t_2+B+y\), so both prediction loadings equal \(\eta=B/R\).  Completing the population ridge square gives
\[
 L_j=\mathbb E_nY_t(0)^2
 -\frac{B^2}{t_j+B+\operatorname{Var}(e_j)},
\]
and hence \(L_1=L_2\) at the tied limit.  Along the stated local calibration, put
\[
 \delta_n=\frac{R^2}{B^2}\frac d{\sqrt n},
 \qquad t_{2,n}=t_2-\delta_n.
\]
Then \(t_{2,n}>0\) eventually and
\[
 L_1-L_2
 =\frac{B^2}{R-\delta_n}-\frac{B^2}{R}
 =\frac d{\sqrt n}\frac{R}{R-\delta_n}
 =\frac d{\sqrt n}+O(n^{-1}).
\]
Thus \(\sqrt n(L_1-L_2)=d+O(n^{-1/2})\), proving the local-gap premise without changing either bridge identity.

At the tied limit set \(U=(1-\eta)F+e_0\).  Centering the difference of the two ridge losses gives
\[
 D=-2\eta U(e_1-e_2)
   +\eta^2(e_1^2-e_2^2+y-x).
\]
The donor means are \(c_j\mu\), so the bridge sensitivities and pre-ATT scores reduce to
\[
 \psi_1=-K(F+e_2)(e_0-e_1),
 \qquad
 \psi_2=-K(F+e_1)(e_0-e_2),
 \qquad K=\frac\mu B.
\]
The post residuals are
\[
 v_1=e_0-e_1+\xi,
 \qquad v_2=e_0-e_2+\xi.
\]
All displayed processes are independent over time, so their long-run covariances equal their one-period covariances and the pre and post Gaussian limits are independent.

We now calculate the five quantities used by \(\Gamma\).  The two terms in \(D\) are uncorrelated by the vanishing odd moments of centered Gaussian variables.  Since
\[
 \mathbb E U^2=(1-\eta)^2B+b,
 \quad
 \mathbb E(e_1-e_2)^2=x+y,
 \quad
 \operatorname{Var}(e_1^2-e_2^2)=2(x^2+y^2),
\]
we get
\[
 \sigma_D^2
 =4\eta^2\{(1-\eta)^2B+b\}(x+y)
  +2\eta^4(x^2+y^2).
\]
For the first covariance, conditioning first on \((F,e_0)\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E\!\left[(e_1-e_2)(F+e_2)(e_0-e_1)\mid F,e_0\right]
 =-xF-ye_0.
\]
The quadratic part of \(D\) has zero covariance with \(\psi_1\), again by odd Gaussian moments.  Therefore
\[
 c_{D1}=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_1)
 =-2\eta K\{(1-\eta)Bx+by\}.
\]
The analogous conditional calculation for role two yields
\[
 c_{D2}=\operatorname{Cov}(D,A_2)
 =2\eta K\{(1-\eta)By+bx\}.
\]
Finally, independence of the factors in each product gives
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(A_1)=K^2(B+y)(b+x),
 \quad
 \operatorname{Var}(A_2)=K^2(B+x)(b+y),
\]
and
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(R_1)=b+x+\zeta,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(R_2)=b+y+\zeta.
\]
Thus
\[
 V_1=K^2(B+y)(b+x)+r(b+x+\zeta),
 \qquad
 V_2=K^2(B+x)(b+y)+r(b+y+\zeta),
\]
and \(\rho_s=c_{Ds}/\sqrt{\sigma_D^2V_s}\), exactly as asserted by \(\Gamma\).

At the symmetric point \((\mu,f,b,x,y,\zeta,t_1,t_2)=(1,1,1,1,1,1,1,1)\),
\[
 B=2,\quad R=4,\quad\eta=K=\frac12,\quad
 \sigma_D^2=\frac{13}{4},\quad c_{D1}=-1,\quad c_{D2}=1,
 \quad V_1=V_2=\frac32+3r.
\]
Hence \(\rho_1=-\rho_2\).  For every finite local gap, Gaussian regression on \(D=\sigma_DX\) gives
\[
 \mathbb E\{A_{J(d)}+\sqrt rR_{J(d)}\}
 =\frac{c_{D2}-c_{D1}}{\sigma_D}\phi(k)
 =\frac{2}{\sigma_D}\phi(k)>0,
\]
while \(\texttt{thm:wald-symmetry-frontier}\) gives exact symmetric coverage for every \(k\).  Moreover \(B/\sqrt{t_1t_2}=2>\kappa\), \(\sigma_D^2=13/4>\nu\), and \(V_s>3/2>\nu\).  The stipulated bound on \(C_{\mathrm{mom}}\) gives the strict Gaussian moment inequality, so this point is legal for every \(r>0\).

At the asymmetric point in the statement,
\[
 B=2,\quad R=4,\quad\eta=K=\frac12,
 \quad \frac{B}{\sqrt{t_1t_2}}=\frac{10}{3},
\]
and substitution into the formulas just proved gives
\[
 \sigma_D^2=\frac{161}{100},\qquad
 c_{D1}=-\frac{19}{100},\qquad
 c_{D2}=\frac{91}{100},
\]
\[
 V_1=\frac14\frac{19}{5}\frac3{10}
      +\frac1{10}\frac4{10}=\frac{13}{40},
 \qquad
 V_2=\frac14\frac{11}{5}\frac{19}{10}
      +\frac1{10}(2)=\frac{249}{200}.
\]
Thus
\[
 \rho_1=-0.2626630497187030329\ldots,
 \qquad
 \rho_2=0.6427525060282437885\ldots,
 \qquad \rho_1^2<\rho_2^2.
\]
The inequalities \(10/3>\kappa\), \(161/100>\nu\), \(13/40>\nu\), and \(249/200>\nu\), together with the stated strict Gaussian moment bound, prove legality.  For \(d/\sigma_D=-1\), one has \(k=1\).  With \(z=\Phi^{-1}(0.95)\), direct substitution into the already proved one-dimensional integral gives
\[
 C_z(1)=0.8858209104904335667026974385\ldots.
\]
For completeness, this decimal is obtained without simulation by substituting the exact rational covariances above into the two error-function integrals, truncating at \(|x|=12\), whose omitted probability is at most \(2\Phi(-12)<4\times10^{-33}\), and evaluating the compact integrals at sixty-decimal working precision.  Repeating the calculation after subdividing each compact interval gives the displayed digits.  Independently of numerical quadrature, \(k>0\) and \(\rho_1^2-\rho_2^2<0\), so the strict sign theorem proves strict undercoverage analytically.

At this point \(R^2/B^2=4\), hence \(t_{2,n}=1/5-4d/\sqrt n\), as claimed.  Every bridge, variance, moment, and positivity expression above is continuous in \((\theta,d)\) wherever \(t_{2,n}>0\).  All legality inequalities at the asymmetric point are strict, and so are \(k>0\) and \(\rho_1^2<\rho_2^2\).  They therefore persist on a relatively open neighborhood of \((\theta,d)\) in the tied manifold crossed with the local-drift line, and they persist eventually along every corresponding local array.  The sign theorem gives strict undercoverage throughout that neighborhood.  Exchanging labels exchanges the squared-correlation ordering.  Keeping the roles fixed and reversing the sign of \(d\) changes the sign of \(k\), so the same sign theorem gives strict overcoverage.
